revise.gpgSign.note: It decides signing in both directions: git-revise re-creates every commit it rewrites, target and descendants alike, whose signed state differs from this setting, so with it false (the default when `commit.gpgSign` is unset too) a run strips existing signatures even from commits it does not otherwise change. With `gpg.format = ssh` it signs with `gpg.ssh.program`; any other format goes through `gpg.program`.

revise.rerere.defaultDescription: the value of `rerere.enabled`; when that is unset too, true exactly when the repository's `rr-cache` directory exists (`git rev-parse --git-path rr-cache`, which linked worktrees share with the main one).
revise.rerere.description: Whether git-revise replays and records conflict resolutions through git's rerere cache. Read once per conflicted file; when false no resolution is replayed or recorded. When a recorded resolution exists, `rerere.autoUpdate` decides whether it is applied without asking (false prompts `Apply recorded resolution? (y/N)`), which differs from what that key means to git itself.
